Maria H: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak on the canary pool we're seeing a ~35% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for RAG chat flows that include structured outputs + long convo prefixes. perf dashboards spiking. :eyes:
Ben K: Ugh. Is this correlated with the new kernel fallback ordering or the batching heuristic change?
Maria H: Looks like both. Kernel picker prefers the new fused-attn kernel for short sequences, but it forces a different kv-key fingerprint path for the long-prefix codepath.
Akash P: Can you paste the numbers? Even ballpark.
Maria H: Sure — sampled from canary over last 2h:
```
workload: rag-chat-qa
prefix_cache.hits: 12.4k
prefix_cache.requests: 19.0k
hitrate: 65.3%  # was ~100.0% before
avg_latency_p50: +18ms
evictions/sec: 14 -> 112
key_generation.time_p95: +9ms
```
Dana L: Evictions jump is scary. That explains tail latency. Are we accidentally changing key canonicalization?
Maria H: Exactly — the new keyer path uses per-tensor hash + layer-order tag to avoid collision in fused kernels. That produced slightly different key strings for convo prefixes with structured fields, so warm-start matching failed.
Will T: Hmm, so two effects: different kernel picks change how we serialize prefix chunks, and batching changes affect ordering which changes keying if we include seq ids.
Michelle S: Can we reproduce locally with a small trace? If we can create a deterministic snippet we can test three keyers (old canonical, new hashed, and a normalized canonical) and measure hit-rate.
Ben K: I pushed a small script to the repo that replays canary traces and prints key diffs. Usage:
```
./tools/replay_trace --trace rag_chat_trace_2026-02-12 --compare-keyers old,new,normalized
```
Maria H: Ran that. Output shows ~40% of prefix keys differed between old and new for messages containing structured JSON-ish chunks (weird nesting + role metadata).
Akash P: So structured outputs are sensitive. Could be whitespace/order of metadata in serialization. We should standardize serialization (stable JSON stringify) before hashing.
Dana L: Agreed. Also consider making the keyer stable against batching reorder by removing ephemeral seq ids.
Will T: Alternative mitigation: fallback to old keyer for canary until we fix canonicalization. This will restore hit-rate quickly.
Maria H: I +1 that. But we need a canary plan: revert kernel ordering OR keep kernel, revert keyer change to old canonical, run canary 4h, validate hit-rate and latency.
Michelle S: I can run the rollback for keyer in canary. If metrics look good after 30m, we can roll to prod gate.
infra-bot: deploy-bot triggered: rollout/keyer-revert/canary started by Michelle S at 2026-02-18T14:03:21Z
Ben K: Also request QA: add a unit test that normalizes structured prefixes (canonical JSON + sorted keys + trimmed whitespace) so future keyers don't regress.
Akash P: I'll add that test and a small fuzz harness that generates nested metadata permutations.
Maria H: Quick profiling note: we saw kernel-level hotpath skew — the new fused kernel increases throughput on short sequences but because cache missed more, overall token cost went up. So it's a net negative for these RAG-chat workloads.
Dana L: We should also add a metric: prefix_key_stability.rate which counts identical keys between request and warm-start candidate in cache for 1h windows. That will catch this class of regressions automatically.
Will T: Agree. Adding to roadmap: 1) stabilize serialization, 2) unit tests + fuzz, 3) metric + alert, 4) canary revert then reintroduce after fixes.
Maria H: Action items:
- Michelle S: revert keyer on canary (in progress)
- Akash P: add canonicalizer + unit tests (ETA end of day)
- Ben K: extend replay tool to show batching-order diffs
- Dana L: add prefix_key_stability metric and dashboard tile
- Will T: coordinate roll plan for kernel reintroduce after fixes

Ben K: Cool. Keep the thread updated with canary numbers. If hit-rate doesn't recover within 30m after revert, escalate.
Maria H: Will do — posting a follow-up when canary finishes: current baseline pre-revert hit-rate ~65%. Target is >95%. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: rollout/keyer-revert/canary succeeded (canary nodes healthy) at 2026-02-18T14:38:02Z
Maria H: Canary numbers are in — immediate improvement: hit-rate back to 98.7%, evictions down to baseline, latency p50 back to normal. Will open PR with canonicalizer + tests and link here.
Akash P: PR #2389 opened: canonical-json-keyer + fuzz tests.
Dana L: Dashboard PR for prefix_key_stability created and added alert (SEV3) if stability drops >10% over 5m.
Will T: Great. Postmortem/notes for release notes later. Thanks team.
Maria H: Thanks all — closing for now, will reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
